claim: Preprocessing video data is computationally expensive, but preprocessing once and reusing the results across epochs eliminates redundant computation and reduces overall cost.
falsifier: In a multi-epoch training loop with video data, preprocess all videos once before training and reuse the results; measure preprocessing time per epoch compared to per-epoch preprocessing.

conditions: Video preprocessing involves expensive operations (frame extraction, object tracking, annotation using local dense networks on GPUs)
The same video data is used across multiple training epochs
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the video understanding workload and the specific preprocessing pipeline described

title: Preprocessing video data once for Elimination of redundant preprocessing
